result.topic_en: A list of proposed general results (marked at the top by another hand as largely false) on the error in summing positive sequences, maximum versus average orders (divisor function, primes), and a Tauberian-type comparison of power series.
result.transcription:
Hardy [?] old [?] : results largely false
Add Ms a 94^{18 (7)} (7)

All variables considered in the following results are positive

1. $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots a_n$ can be expressed in terms of $n$ with an error of $O(\max a_n - \min a_n)$. Perhaps we may go even as far as ascertaining the maximum and the minimum of $O$ and it is not possible to go beyond that. e.g.
(i) $d(1) + d(2) + d(3) + \cdots d(n) = n(2\gamma - 1 + \log n) + O(\max d(n))$
$= n(2\gamma - 1 + \log n) + 2^{O\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)}$.
(ii) $\log 2 + \log 3 + \log 5 + \log 7 + \log 11 + \cdots$ to $n$ terms can be expressed in terms of $n$ with an error of $o(1)$ or even $O(n^{-\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon})$; for
$O(\max \log p_n - \min \log p_n) = O(n^{-\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon})$.
2. The maximum order of [-of-] $a_n = \max. \sqrt[r]{(\text{average order of } a_n^r)}$ for the variable $r$. e.g.
(i) max. $d(n)$ can be shown to be $2^{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}(1+\epsilon)}$
(ii) The maximum order of $\pi(p)$
$= Li(p) + \max. \sqrt[r]{\{\text{average order of } (p-p')^r\}}$
where $p'$ is the prime just less than the prime $p$.
3. If $b_n$ is steadily increasing and if $\max a_n > b_n$, and if $(a_1 e^{-x} + a_2 e^{-2x} + a_3 e^{-3x} + \cdots\cdots)$
$-(b_1 e^{-x} + b_2 e^{-2x} + b_3 e^{-3x} + \cdots\cdots) = O(1)$ as $x \to 0$
then $a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + \cdots a_n$
$= b_1 + b_2 + b_3 + \cdots\cdots b_n + O(\max a_n - \min a_n)$.
4. If in (3) $a_n$ also is steadily increasing, then
$a_n \sim b_n$.

items.quote: $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots a_n$ can be expressed in terms of $n$ with an error of $O(\max a_n - \min a_n)$
items.english: The sum of the first n terms can be expressed as a function of n with error O(max a_n − min a_n).

items.quote: Perhaps we may go even as far as ascertaining the maximum and the minimum of $O$ and it is not possible to go beyond that.
items.english: Perhaps one can even determine the maximum and minimum of the O-term, and one cannot go further.

items.quote: $\log 2 + \log 3 + \log 5 + \log 7 + \log 11 + \cdots$ to $n$ terms can be expressed in terms of $n$ with an error of $o(1)$ or even $O(n^{-\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon})$
items.english: The sum of logs of the first n primes can be expressed in terms of n with error o(1) or even O(n^{-1/2+ε}).

items.quote: The maximum order of [-of-] $a_n = \max. \sqrt[r]{(\text{average order of } a_n^r)}$ for the variable $r$
items.english: The maximum order of a_n equals the max over r of the r-th root of the average order of a_n^r.

items.quote:
The maximum order of $\pi(p)$
$= Li(p) + \max. \sqrt[r]{\{\text{average order of } (p-p')^r\}}$
items.english: The maximum order of π(p) is Li(p) plus the max over r of the r-th root of the average order of (p−p')^r, p' the previous prime.

items.quote:
If $b_n$ is steadily increasing and if $\max a_n > b_n$, and if $(a_1 e^{-x} + a_2 e^{-2x} + a_3 e^{-3x} + \cdots\cdots)$
$-(b_1 e^{-x} + b_2 e^{-2x} + b_3 e^{-3x} + \cdots\cdots) = O(1)$ as $x \to 0$
then $a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + \cdots a_n$
$= b_1 + b_2 + b_3 + \cdots\cdots b_n + O(\max a_n - \min a_n)$.
items.english: If b_n increases, max a_n > b_n, and the two exponential series differ by O(1) as x→0, then the partial sums differ by O(max a_n − min a_n).

items.quote:
If in (3) $a_n$ also is steadily increasing, then
$a_n \sim b_n$.
items.english: If in (3) a_n is also increasing, then a_n is asymptotic to b_n.
